questions.questionText: When driving in dense fog, which lighting should you use?
options: High-beam headlights to pierce the fog.
Low-beam headlights.
Parking lights only.
questions.explanationShort: Always use low-beam headlights in fog.
questions.explanationDetailed: High beams will reflect off the moisture in the fog and create glare, reducing your visibility further. Low beams direct light downward onto the road surface.

questions.questionText: If your vehicle begins to hydroplane on a wet road, what is the safest immediate action?
options: Brake firmly to regain traction.
Turn the steering wheel sharply in the direction of the skid.
Gradually ease your foot off the accelerator.
questions.explanationShort: Ease off the gas; do not brake or turn sharply.
questions.explanationDetailed: Hydroplaning occurs when tires ride on a layer of water instead of the road. Braking hard or turning sharply can cause a complete loss of control. Easing off the gas allows the tires to eventually reconnect with the road.

questions.questionText: When you approach a school bus with flashing red lights stopped on a two-lane road, you must:
options: Stop until the red lights stop flashing.
Slow down to 15 mph and proceed with caution.
Stop only if children are actively crossing the street.
questions.explanationShort: You must stop until the flashing red lights turn off.
questions.explanationDetailed: Flashing red lights on a school bus mean you must stop from either direction on a two-lane road. You may only proceed once the lights stop flashing and the bus begins to move.

questions.questionText: Under California law, when may you legally leave a child aged 6 or younger unattended in a motor vehicle?
options: Only if the windows are cracked open.
If the engine is running and the air conditioning is on.
Only if they are supervised by someone at least 12 years old.
questions.explanationShort: They must be supervised by someone 12 or older.
questions.explanationDetailed: It is illegal to leave a child 6 years old or younger unattended in a motor vehicle unless supervised by a person who is at least 12 years old, due to extreme temperature risks and safety hazards.

questions.questionText: What does the Basic Speed Law mandate?
options: You must never drive faster than is safe for current conditions.
You must always drive at the posted speed limit.
You may drive 5 mph over the limit if passing.
questions.explanationShort: Never drive faster than conditions safely allow.
questions.explanationDetailed: Regardless of the posted limit, your speed must be adjusted for weather, traffic, road conditions, and visibility. The posted limit indicates the maximum speed under ideal conditions.

questions.questionText: A solid double yellow line in the center of a two-way roadway indicates:
options: Passing is permitted if the way is clear.
Vehicles in both directions are prohibited from passing.
You are approaching a one-way street.
questions.explanationShort: Solid double yellow lines mean no passing.
questions.explanationDetailed: You may not cross solid double yellow lines to pass another vehicle. You may only cross them to make a permitted left turn into or out of a driveway or alley.

questions.questionText: What action is required when you encounter a flashing red traffic signal?
options: Slow down and proceed with extreme caution.
Stop completely, then proceed when it is safe.
Yield to pedestrians, but stopping is not required.
questions.explanationShort: Treat a flashing red light like a stop sign.
questions.explanationDetailed: A flashing red traffic signal means exactly the same thing as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, yield the right-of-way, and proceed only when safe.

questions.questionText: A diamond-shaped sign on the roadway is exclusively used for:
options: Warning drivers of potential hazards ahead.
Indicating regulatory speed limits.
Providing directions to nearby hospitals.
questions.explanationShort: Diamond-shaped signs provide warnings.
questions.explanationDetailed: Yellow diamond-shaped signs alert drivers to specific road conditions or hazards ahead, such as a sharp curve, pedestrian crossing, or slippery road.

questions.questionText: When you see a white rectangular sign indicating 'DO NOT PASS', it means:
options: You cannot pass vehicles on a two-lane road.
You are entering a school zone.
You must exit the highway immediately.
questions.explanationShort: Do not overtake other vehicles.
questions.explanationDetailed: White rectangular signs are regulatory. This sign explicitly prohibits you from overtaking and passing other vehicles in that specific zone.

questions.questionText: If a traffic signal is completely unlit due to a power outage, how should you proceed?
options: Yield to the vehicle on your right and proceed without stopping.
Treat the intersection as a four-way stop.
Follow the vehicle ahead of you closely through the intersection.
questions.explanationShort: Treat an unlit signal as a four-way stop.
questions.explanationDetailed: When a traffic signal is blacked out, all vehicles must come to a complete stop. You must then proceed using the standard right-of-way rules for a four-way stop intersection.

questions.questionText: Two vehicles arrive at an intersection with four stop signs at the same time. Who must yield?
options: The vehicle traveling straight.
The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle making a turn yields to the vehicle traveling straight.
questions.explanationShort: The vehicle on the left must yield.
questions.explanationDetailed: At a four-way stop, if two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. The driver on the left must yield.

questions.questionText: When attempting to make a left turn on a solid green light, you must:
options: Proceed immediately; you have the right-of-way.
Yield to oncoming traffic that is close enough to be dangerous.
Wait until the light turns yellow before turning.
questions.explanationShort: Yield to oncoming traffic before turning left.
questions.explanationDetailed: A solid green light permits a left turn, but it is unprotected. You must pull forward and yield to any oncoming vehicles and pedestrians before completing the turn.

questions.questionText: If a pedestrian is waiting to cross at an unmarked crosswalk at an intersection, you must:
options: Maintain your speed if there are no painted lines.
Sound your horn to warn the pedestrian.
Yield the right-of-way and let them cross.
questions.explanationShort: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at all intersections.
questions.explanationDetailed: Crosswalks exist at all intersections, whether they are marked with painted lines or not. You must always yield to pedestrians crossing the street at an intersection.

questions.questionText: You are approaching a T-intersection from the terminating road (the road that ends). There are no stop signs. Who has the right-of-way?
options: You have the right-of-way because you are entering the intersection.
Traffic on the continuing through-road has the right-of-way.
The vehicle traveling at the faster speed.
questions.explanationShort: Yield to traffic on the through-road.
questions.explanationDetailed: At a T-intersection without signs or signals, vehicles on the road that ends must yield the right-of-way to vehicles traveling on the continuing cross street.

questions.questionText: When entering a public road from a private driveway, who possesses the right-of-way?
options: The vehicle entering the public road.
All approaching vehicles and pedestrians on the public road.
The first vehicle to reach the curb line.
questions.explanationShort: Yield to all traffic and pedestrians on the public road.
questions.explanationDetailed: Before entering a public road from an alley, driveway, or parking lot, you must stop and yield to all pedestrians and vehicles already on the road or sidewalk.

questions.questionText: Unless otherwise posted, what is the standard speed limit in a business or residential district?
options: 25 mph
30 mph
35 mph
questions.explanationShort: The limit is 25 mph in business and residential areas.
questions.explanationDetailed: To protect pedestrians and local traffic, California law sets a default speed limit of 25 mph in all residential and business districts unless signage specifies otherwise.

questions.questionText: What is the recommended minimum following distance you should maintain under ideal driving conditions?
options: One car length for every 10 mph of speed.
The 'three-second' rule.
50 feet.
questions.explanationShort: Use the three-second rule.
questions.explanationDetailed: To avoid rear-end collisions, pick a fixed object ahead. When the vehicle in front of you passes it, count 'one-thousand-one, one-thousand-two, one-thousand-three.' If you pass the object before finishing, you are following too closely.

questions.questionText: When driving on a wet road, how should you adjust your speed?
options: Reduce your speed by 5 to 10 mph.
Cut your speed in half.
Maintain the posted speed limit but turn on your wipers.
questions.explanationShort: Slow down by 5 to 10 mph on wet roads.
questions.explanationDetailed: Wet roads have less traction. To maintain control and avoid hydroplaning, you should reduce your speed by about 5 to 10 miles per hour compared to dry conditions.

questions.questionText: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit when driving through an intersection with obstructed visibility (a 'blind' intersection)?
options: 15 mph
25 mph
20 mph
questions.explanationShort: The limit is 15 mph for blind intersections.
questions.explanationDetailed: An intersection is 'blind' if there are no stop signs and you cannot see 100 feet in either direction during the last 100 feet before crossing. The limit is 15 mph to allow time to stop.

questions.questionText: When passing a school building or school grounds while children are present, what is the maximum speed limit unless posted otherwise?
options: 15 mph
25 mph
35 mph
questions.explanationShort: The school zone speed limit is typically 25 mph.
questions.explanationDetailed: When children are outside or crossing the street near a school, the speed limit is 25 mph. Some school zones may have lower posted limits, but 25 mph is the standard maximum.

questions.questionText: When approaching a roundabout, in which direction must you drive?
options: Clockwise.
Counter-clockwise.
Straight through the center island.
questions.explanationShort: Traffic in a roundabout travels counter-clockwise.
questions.explanationDetailed: All vehicles entering a roundabout must yield to traffic already in the circle and proceed to the right, driving in a counter-clockwise direction.

questions.questionText: You are waiting in an intersection to complete a left turn. Your wheels should be:
options: Pointed straight ahead.
Turned slightly to the left.
Turned completely to the left.
questions.explanationShort: Keep your wheels straight until you begin the turn.
questions.explanationDetailed: If your wheels are turned left while waiting, a rear-end collision could push your vehicle directly into the path of oncoming traffic. Keep them straight until it is safe to turn.

questions.questionText: If you find yourself in an intersection when a traffic light turns red, you should:
options: Back up behind the crosswalk immediately.
Stop exactly where you are.
Continue through the intersection and clear it safely.
questions.explanationShort: Clear the intersection safely.
questions.explanationDetailed: You must never stop in the middle of an intersection. If you have already crossed the limit line when the light turns red, proceed through to clear the intersection.

questions.questionText: A red arrow pointing right on a traffic signal means:
options: You may turn right after coming to a complete stop, unless a sign prohibits it.
You must stop and you cannot turn right until the light turns green.
You may turn right without stopping if the intersection is clear.
questions.explanationShort: No turning on a red arrow.
questions.explanationDetailed: Unlike a solid red circle, a red arrow means you must stop and you may NOT turn in the direction of the arrow until it turns green.

questions.questionText: Yellow lines painted in a crosshatch pattern inside an intersection indicate:
options: A pedestrian safety zone; do not block.
An area you must not enter if traffic will force you to stop there.
A designated loading zone.
questions.explanationShort: Do not block the intersection.
questions.explanationDetailed: These markings, often accompanied by 'Keep Clear' signs, indicate that you must not enter the intersection unless you have enough space to cross completely without stopping.

questions.questionText: When are you permitted to drive in a bicycle lane?
options: When traffic is heavily congested.
When you are within 200 feet of an intersection and preparing to turn right.
You are never permitted to drive in a bicycle lane.
questions.explanationShort: Only to prepare for a right turn within 200 feet.
questions.explanationDetailed: You may enter a bike lane to make a right turn, but you must not drive in it for more than 200 feet before the intersection, and you must yield to bicycles.

questions.questionText: On a highway with three lanes traveling in the same direction, which lane should you choose for the smoothest driving?
options: The far-left lane (Lane 1).
The middle lane (Lane 2).
The far-right lane (Lane 3).
questions.explanationShort: The middle lane offers the smoothest flow.
questions.explanationDetailed: The far-left lane is for passing or faster traffic. The far-right lane is for slower traffic, entering, and exiting. The middle lane generally provides the smoothest flow.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of a center lane marked by solid yellow lines on the outside and broken yellow lines on the inside?
options: It is a designated passing lane for both directions.
It is a shared center left-turn lane.
It is an express lane for carpools.
questions.explanationShort: It is a shared left-turn lane.
questions.explanationDetailed: This lane is reserved for vehicles making left turns (or U-turns where permitted) from either direction. You may only drive in this lane for a maximum of 200 feet.

questions.questionText: When crossing a solid white line on a highway, you should:
options: Proceed without signaling.
Cross it quickly to minimize disruption.
Avoid crossing it unless absolutely necessary.
questions.explanationShort: Solid white lines discourage lane changes.
questions.explanationDetailed: Solid white lines separate lanes of traffic traveling in the same direction. They indicate that lane changes are discouraged due to potential hazards, though not strictly illegal.

questions.questionText: High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) lanes are marked with which symbol?
options: A white diamond.
A yellow circle.
A white shield.
questions.explanationShort: HOV lanes are marked with a white diamond.
questions.explanationDetailed: Carpool or HOV lanes are reserved for vehicles with a minimum number of occupants, or specific low-emission vehicles. They are clearly marked with a painted white diamond on the road surface.

questions.questionText: When parking your vehicle facing downhill on a street with a curb, how should you point your front wheels?
options: Away from the curb.
Straight ahead.
Turned toward the curb.
questions.explanationShort: Turn wheels toward the curb on a downhill.
questions.explanationDetailed: If your brakes fail on a downhill slope, turning the wheels toward the curb will cause the vehicle to roll into the curb and stop, preventing it from rolling into traffic.

questions.questionText: What does a curb painted blue indicate?
options: Parking is permitted for only 15 minutes.
Parking is restricted for disabled persons with a special placard or license plate.
The area is a designated bus stop.
questions.explanationShort: Blue curbs are for disabled parking only.
questions.explanationDetailed: A blue curb designates parking exclusively for persons with disabilities. A valid disabled placard or special license plate must be visibly displayed on the vehicle.

questions.questionText: When parallel parked, your vehicle's wheels must be within what distance from the curb?
options: 18 inches
24 inches
36 inches
questions.explanationShort: Within 18 inches of the curb.
questions.explanationDetailed: California law requires that when parallel parked on a level street, the wheels of your vehicle must be parallel to and within 18 inches of the curb.

questions.questionText: When parking facing uphill on a street with NO curb, how should you point your front wheels?
options: Turned toward the edge of the road.
Turned away from the edge of the road.
Straight ahead.
questions.explanationShort: Turn wheels toward the side of the road.
questions.explanationDetailed: When there is no curb (uphill or downhill), always turn your wheels toward the edge of the road so that if the vehicle rolls, it will roll off the roadway, not into traffic.

questions.questionText: What does a curb painted white indicate?
options: Parking for commercial vehicles loading or unloading only.
Stop only long enough to pick up or drop off passengers or mail.
Parking is completely prohibited at all times.
questions.explanationShort: White curbs are for passenger loading.
questions.explanationDetailed: A white painted curb means you may stop only for the immediate loading or unloading of passengers, or to deposit mail in an adjacent mailbox.

questions.questionText: When a large truck is making a right turn, what hazard should you be most aware of?
options: The truck will accelerate rapidly through the turn.
The truck may need to swing wide to the left to complete the right turn.
The truck will stop completely before turning.
questions.explanationShort: Large trucks make wide right turns.
questions.explanationDetailed: Large vehicles often must swing wide into the adjacent left lane to prevent their rear wheels from jumping the curb. Never try to squeeze past a truck on the right when it is turning.

questions.questionText: If an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights and a siren while you are in an intersection, you should:
options: Stop immediately in the intersection.
Pull over to the right side of the intersection and stop.
Continue through the intersection, then pull over to the right and stop.
questions.explanationShort: Clear the intersection before pulling over.
questions.explanationDetailed: Never stop in the middle of an intersection. Proceed safely through the intersection, then immediately pull over to the right edge of the road and stop.

questions.questionText: When sharing the road with a light rail vehicle (trolley), you should:
options: Pass the trolley on the left side.
Never turn in front of an approaching light rail vehicle.
Treat it exactly like a passenger car.
questions.explanationShort: Never turn in front of a light rail vehicle.
questions.explanationDetailed: Light rail vehicles cannot stop quickly and have limited visibility. Always verify that a turn is completely clear of approaching trolleys before crossing the tracks.

questions.questionText: Motorcycles are permitted to 'lane split' (drive between two lanes of traffic) in California. What is your responsibility?
options: You must move to the shoulder to let them pass.
You should honk to alert them of your presence.
You must check your mirrors and blind spots carefully before changing lanes.
questions.explanationShort: Check blind spots frequently for motorcycles.
questions.explanationDetailed: Lane splitting is legal in California. Because motorcycles are small and can appear suddenly between lanes, you must be extremely diligent about checking blind spots before any maneuver.

questions.questionText: You are driving on a two-lane road and a bicyclist is riding ahead of you in your lane. How should you pass?
options: Honk your horn and squeeze past them in the same lane.
Wait until oncoming traffic is clear, then pass leaving at least 3 feet of clearance.
Drive on the right shoulder to pass them.
questions.explanationShort: Leave at least 3 feet of space when passing bicycles.
questions.explanationDetailed: By law, you must provide a minimum clearance of 3 feet when overtaking a bicycle. If 3 feet is not possible, you must slow down and wait until it is safe to pass.

questions.questionText: When is it legal to send or read a text message while driving?
options: When you are stopped at a red light.
Only if using a hands-free voice-to-text system.
Under no circumstances.
questions.explanationShort: Only via hands-free, voice-operated systems.
questions.explanationDetailed: It is illegal to hold a phone to read, write, or send text messages while driving. You may only use a device if it is mounted and operated entirely hands-free or via voice commands.

questions.questionText: To scan your surroundings effectively while driving, you should:
options: Keep your eyes fixed strictly on the vehicle directly in front of you.
Constantly sweep your eyes back and forth, near and far.
Look mainly at the right side of the road.
questions.explanationShort: Keep your eyes moving to scan for hazards.
questions.explanationDetailed: Good drivers keep their eyes constantly moving. Staring at a single fixed object causes 'highway hypnosis' and reduces your awareness of surrounding hazards.

questions.questionText: What is the primary danger of driving while feeling fatigued or drowsy?
options: You may drive faster than the speed limit.
Your reaction time slows down and your judgment is impaired.
Your vehicle will consume more fuel.
questions.explanationShort: Fatigue severely impairs reaction time and judgment.
questions.explanationDetailed: Drowsy driving is extremely dangerous. It mimics the effects of alcohol impairment, reducing your ability to make split-second decisions and slowing your physical reaction time.

questions.questionText: When changing lanes, the very last step before steering into the new lane is to:
options: Turn on your turn signal.
Check your rearview mirror.
Turn your head to check your blind spot.
questions.explanationShort: Always physically check your blind spot.
questions.explanationDetailed: Mirrors do not show everything. After signaling and checking mirrors, you must briefly turn your head to look over your shoulder into the blind spot to ensure the space is empty.

questions.questionText: In California, it is illegal for a person 21 years of age or older to drive with a Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of:
options: 0.08% or higher.
0.05% or higher.
0.01% or higher.
questions.explanationShort: The legal limit for adults is 0.08%.
questions.explanationDetailed: For adults 21 and older operating a regular passenger vehicle, driving with a BAC of 0.08% or higher is a DUI offense. However, you can still be impaired and arrested at lower levels.

questions.questionText: If your right wheels drift off the paved road onto the dirt shoulder, you should:
options: Brake hard and yank the steering wheel to the left.
Grip the wheel firmly, ease off the gas, and steer back onto the pavement gently once slowed.
Accelerate to regain traction before turning back.
questions.explanationShort: Ease off the gas and steer back gently.
questions.explanationDetailed: Over-correcting (yanking the wheel) or braking hard on dirt can cause the vehicle to flip or spin into oncoming traffic. Maintain control, slow down, and merge back carefully.

questions.questionText: If you experience a sudden tire blowout on the highway, your first reaction should be to:
options: Slam on the brakes to stop as fast as possible.
Hold the steering wheel tightly and keep the vehicle going straight.
Quickly steer off the road into the ditch.
questions.explanationShort: Hold the wheel firmly and maintain your path.
questions.explanationDetailed: A blowout will pull the vehicle hard to the side of the blown tire. Braking hard will exacerbate this pull. Hold the wheel tight, ease off the gas, and brake gently only after regaining control.

questions.questionText: If your vehicle is sinking in water, what is the best way to escape?
options: Wait for the vehicle to fill with water so the pressure equalizes before opening the door.
Roll down or break a window immediately to escape.
Call 911 and wait for emergency services to arrive.
questions.explanationShort: Escape through a window immediately.
questions.explanationDetailed: Water pressure will rapidly make doors impossible to open. The electrical system may fail quickly, so immediately roll down or break a side window (not the windshield) to escape.

questions.questionText: What should you do if your brakes fail while you are driving?
options: Turn the engine off immediately.
Shift to a lower gear and pump the brake pedal rapidly.
Pull the parking brake up as hard and fast as you can.
questions.explanationShort: Shift to a lower gear and pump the brakes.
questions.explanationDetailed: Pumping the brakes may build up enough fluid pressure to stop the vehicle. Shifting to a lower gear allows the engine to help slow the vehicle down.

questions.questionText: If you are involved in a collision and there are no injuries, you should:
options: Leave your vehicles exactly where they are until police arrive.
Move your vehicles out of the traffic lane if it is safe to do so.
Wait inside your vehicle in the middle of the road.
questions.explanationShort: Move vehicles out of traffic if there are no injuries.
questions.explanationDetailed: If a collision causes property damage only and the vehicles can be moved, you must move them out of the traffic lanes to prevent further accidents and traffic congestion.
